messages.text: Martinez releases statement to clarify outburst - but does not apologise

metadata.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology.
metadata.content: Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Lisandro Martinez: Man Utd defender releases statement to clarify outburst but does not apologise Man Utd defender Lisandro Martinez called out the club's hierarchy after their Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid; Martinez said he had expected more from "upstairs", singling out technical director Jason Wilcox Wednesday 14 October 2026 23:53, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Daily Mail’s Craig Hope and John Cross from The Mirror give their views on Lisandro Martinez's statement Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has clarified his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid in a statement - but stopped short of an apology. Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Madrid, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad, said he expected more from "upstairs" and singled out technical director Jason Wilcox. But 24 hours on from his astonishing post-match interview, the Argentina international released a statement on Instagram on Wednesday night to clear up his comments. metadata.summary: England's Red Roses have made four changes to their starting XV for their game against Canada in Rugby's WXV Global Series.
metadata.content: England's Red Roses: John Mitchell makes four changes to starting XV for Canada WXV Global Series Test in Toronto | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England's Red Roses: John Mitchell makes four changes to starting XV for Canada WXV Global Series Test in Toronto John Mitchell makes four changes to Red Roses side to face Canada in Toronto; Amy Cokayne, Tatyana Heard, Hannah Botterman, Abi Burton in; Watch Australia vs New Zealand in Bledisloe Cup Test on Saturday live on Sky Sports Main Event from 6am Wednesday 14 October 2026 19:05, UK Image: Amy Cokayne has returned to the Red Roses starting XV as one of four changes to face Canada in Toronto England's Red Roses have made four changes to their starting XV for their game against Canada in Rugby's WXV Global Series. Experienced hooker Amy Cokayne, centre Tatyana Heard, loosehead prop Hannah Botterman and back-row Abi Burton are each brought in to start in Toronto by head coach John Mitchell. The Red Roses face Canada on Saturday a month after t hey were held to an entertaining 26-26 draw in Exeter , and having most-recently needed a try in the final play of the match to beat New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham. metadata.summary: Laurent Mekies has signed a five-year contract extension to continue as Red Bull team principal and chief executive until 2031.
metadata.content: Laurent Mekies: Red Bull team principal signs contract extension to 2031 and vows recent wins 'only the beginning' | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Laurent Mekies: Red Bull team principal signs contract extension to 2031 and vows recent wins 'only the beginning' Red Bull announce extended five-year contract for team boss Laurent Mekies, who replaced Christian Horner in the role last season; watch every session of the United States GP in Austin on October 23-25, live on Sky Sports F1 Wednesday 14 October 2026 17:56, UK Image: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies Laurent Mekies has signed a five-year contract extension to continue as Red Bull team principal and chief executive until 2031. Mekies joined the team from sister outfit Racing Bulls in July 2025 after Christian Horner was sacked following 20 years in charge. News of Mekies' contract renewal comes in the wake of Red Bull claiming their first two wins of the season, both courtesy of Max Verstappen, over the past fortnight in Malaysia and Singapore.
